                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue and worsening abdominal pain for 4 weeks. He also reports excessive night sweats and a 5.4-kg (12-lb) weight loss during this time. He has a neck swelling for 4 days. Physical examination shows a nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node. There is splenomegaly. A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Analysis of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Adult T-cell lymphoma
opb. Burkitt lymphoma
opc. Follicular lymphoma
opd. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
ope. Hodgkin lymphoma

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, neck swelling, and splenomegaly, along with the presence of a nontender, enlarged, fixed supraclavicular lymph node and massively enlarged lymph nodes on CT, suggest a lymphoproliferative disorder. The biopsy showing CD20 positive lymphocytes indicates a B-cell lymphoma. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most likely diagnosis, as it is a common aggressive B-cell lymphoma that presents with systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy. Follicular lymphoma is less likely due to its typically indolent nature and different clinical presentation. Hodgkin lymphoma is unlikely because it usually shows Reed-Sternberg cells and not CD20 positivity. Burkitt lymphoma, while a B-cell lymphoma, typically presents with a very rapid growth and often involves the jaw or abdomen, not the described pattern. Adult T-cell lymphoma is ruled out due to the CD20 positivity, which is a marker for B-cells, not T-cells. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, do not directly support or contradict the diagnosis of DLBCL, but the presence of CD20 positive lymphocytes is a key diagnostic feature for B-cell lymphomas, supporting the diagnosis of DLBCL.
